summary.headline: Rathi Steel FY26 total income rose ~41.7% to INR716 crore; Q4 PAT INR7.45 crore at 3% margin, with mills still only ~51-52% utilised.
summary.overview: Management reported FY26 total income of about INR716 crore (+41.7% YoY), EBITDA of INR28.9 crore (+18.8%) and PAT of INR12.87 crore (+39.24%, excluding prior-year exceptional items). Q4 total income was INR244.57 crore (+63.3% YoY, +52.7% QoQ), EBITDA INR9.89 crore (+22% YoY, +54% QoQ) and PAT INR7.45 crore, with PAT margin of about 3%. Growth was attributed to the restart of the idle TMT rolling mill in April 2025, which lifted rolling output about 117% to roughly 1,02,000 tons. Utilisation remains low at about 51-52% for both rolling and melting, which management sees as the main lever for margins.

segments.name: Rolling mill (TMT and stainless wire rod)
segments.commentary: Capacity ~2,00,000 tons per annum, utilisation ~51.4% in FY26; output grew ~117% YoY to ~1,02,000 tons after the TMT mill restart. Management did not split volumes between TMT and stainless.

segments.name: Steel melting shop (SMS)
segments.commentary: Capacity ~85,000 tons per annum, utilisation ~53% in FY26 (50-52% cited in opening remarks); about 40-45% backward integrated. Target is ~80% utilisation.

segments.name: Stainless steel vs TMT revenue mix
segments.commentary: Management estimated ~60% of FY26 revenue from B2B (mainly stainless) and ~40% from TMT bars, an approximate figure.

guidance_outlook: Rolling mill utilisation targeted at ~65-70% this year (fallback ~60-65%), up from ~51%.
Steel melting shop utilisation to move from ~50-52% towards ~80%.
Aspiration for ~20-25% average annual growth, using FY25 as base; earlier guidance was ~20% CAGR over three years.
Direct charging on the TMT mill expected to save ~INR3,000-4,000 per ton, or ~6-7% of TMT selling price including yield benefits, on the directly charged volume.
Capex of ~INR20 crore+ a year expected to continue for a few years, mainly replacement and debottlenecking; SMS expansion under study subject to approvals.
Refinancing talks under way with the existing lender at 16% cost of borrowing, with new lenders being explored at lower rates.
capex_capacity: Melting capacity ~85,000 tpa and rolling ~2,00,000 tpa at a ~12.5-acre NCR (Ghaziabad) site; FY26 utilisation ~51-52% for both divisions.
FY26 capex of INR20 crore+, mostly replacement and debottlenecking; the TMT restart cost ~INR5-7 crore in FY25.
Direct charging being implemented on the TMT mill, following its success in stainless wire rod.
SMS capacity expansion being evaluated at costs well below industry benchmarks; a larger melting unit is under consideration subject to demand visibility and statutory clearances.
Rooftop solar feasibility under study, indicatively 1-2 MW; open-access renewable power is over one-fourth of total power consumption.
demand_pricing: Management says domestic steel demand is healthy, with TMT and rebar pricing recovering after a prolonged soft patch.
Imports, mainly from Asia, are pressuring the industry; management says few rebar or stainless long products are imported into NCR, so the direct impact is limited.
Stainless steel pricing comes under pressure above a certain utilisation level; the company is shifting to a more balanced product mix to reduce reliance on any one category.
TMT sold mainly in NCR because freight limits longer-distance sales; stainless also sold in other states.
Institutional buyers are increasingly asking for GreenPro-certified products, which the company obtained for its Rathi Powertech 550 grade TMT bars (CII GreenPro Type-1 Ecolabel).
Fuel costs have roughly doubled over two to three months due to the Iran situation, which management cited as a margin headwind.

qa_highlights.question: What were TMT and stainless volume growth and spreads?
qa_highlights.answer: Management gave no separate TMT and stainless volumes; overall rolled output grew ~117% to ~1,02,000 tons. Margins are expected to improve with higher utilisation, subject to fuel costs.

qa_highlights.question: What is the cost of borrowing and the finance cost reduction target for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Current cost of borrowing is 16% from a single lender. Talks are under way to refinance and secure additional need-based facilities at lower cost; no reduction target was quantified.

qa_highlights.question: What are the GST disputes and how much is under dispute?
qa_highlights.answer: Disputes relate to alleged input ITC issues at various adjudication stages; some are stayed by higher courts. Management does not expect any demand to crystallise. No amount was given.

qa_highlights.question: What are the payment and inventory cycles?
qa_highlights.answer: Average debtor period is ~25-30 days across products (receivables ~1 month). Payables ~60 days; inventory ~25-30 days (about one month overall).

qa_highlights.question: What are the key competitors and how does Rathi compete?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited NCR proximity for delivery, brand recall and distribution network as edges; cost will be at par with peers once direct charging is in place on TMT.

qa_highlights.question: What are the challenges to reach 75-80% utilisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited establishing product acceptance for the restarted TMT mill and stainless supply pressure from IBC-driven acquisitions two years ago, with demand expected to catch up with supply.

risks_watch: Fuel cost spike (Iran-related) eroding the direct-charging saving and the margin recovery.
Stainless steel pricing pressure as utilisation rises, given new supply from IBC acquisitions.
Single-lender dependence at 16% cost of borrowing; refinancing outcome is pending.
Unquantified GST input-credit disputes with adjudication and stays still pending.
Management did not give a Q4 volume split between TMT and stainless, or Q4 raw material cost; key data gaps.
Slow utilisation ramp (51% to 65-70% target) and the 550D premium-grade product push.
Plant ageing; ongoing replacement capex needed.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth and the restart story, but cautious on margins, citing fuel-cost volatility and stainless pricing pressure. Evasive on specifics: the GST dispute amount, TMT vs stainless split, and the finance-cost reduction target were not quantified.
key_quotes: We are proud to be India's first and only stainless steel wire rod manufacturer using direct charging technology where hot billets are directly transferred to rolling mills without reheating.
So, we have a lot of headroom available to improve the capacities further.
We don't foresee any sort of demand fructifying out of it.

financial_highlights.value: ~1 month receivables; ~60 days payables; ~25-30 days inventory

adds.what: Steel melting shop expansion under study (larger melting unit considered, subject to demand visibility and statutory clearances); no size or timing committed
Direct charging implementation on TMT mill (process change, not new capacity)

growth.why: Management aspires to 20-25% average annual growth (held from FY25 base) and targets rolling utilisation of 65-70% in FY27 (from 51.4%), plus SMS utilisation toward 80%; backing is partly specific (idle TMT mill restart already done, direct-charging savings of 6-7%) but no new capacity commissioning or firm orders with timing were given, and SMS expansion remains under study.
